routes.label: Cyanosulfidic (Sutherland/Powner)
routes.note: Encoded via the readable 2-thiooxazole branch (Stairs 2017) because the canonical 2-aminooxazole route (Powner 2009) is paywalled; Powner steps C5 and C7 are 'unread'. Continues into Caimi 2025 polymerisation, which is pond chemistry inside the same surface-pool scenario.

scenario.name: cyanosulfidic
scenario.basis: Patel 2015 (10.1038/nchem.2202, 'Towards a geochemical scenario', Fig. 2): post-impact surface streams and pools leaching a thermally metamorphosed evaporite: HCN and NaCN/KCN, CaNCN -> cyanamide, CaC2 -> acetylene -> cyanoacetylene (Cu-catalysed, >25%), Mg3N2 -> NH3, phosphate from schreibersite/vivianite, hydrosulfide from metal sulfides, Cu(I) cyanocuprates; solar UV; sequential delivery by flow. Urea: Patel 2015 calls it a by-product of the cyanamide step. HSCN from HCN + sulfur per Stairs 2017 (10.1038/ncomms15270). Upper T 150 C: the scenario invokes geothermal/impact heating of dry evaporite; no step here runs above 100 C. Feedstock concentrations are not stated by the sources (INF). Rain stream pH is our assumption.

steps.name: HCN -> glycolaldehyde and glyceraldehyde (trapped as cyanate oxazolidinones), Cu(I) photoredox
steps.yield_text: oxazolidinone 13 (from glycolaldehyde) ~15% on average per 4 HCN; 14 (from glyceraldehyde) 1-5%; ~30% of HCN lost to a black polymer
steps.where: main text, 'neutralized by the addition of hydrochloric acid', 254 nm, 7 h; yields paragraph
steps.notes: The sugars are sequestered by cyanate as oxazolidinones; free glycolaldehyde is not the accumulated product. Temperature and concentrations are in the SI (not read). pH: 'neutralized' (recorded as 7). Patel 2015 reports an H2S-driven variant that gives the free sugars, but its main text gives no yields for it.

steps.name: glycolaldehyde + thiocyanic acid -> 2-thiooxazole
steps.yield_text: 85% (isolated)
steps.where: Results 'Oxazole 4a...'; Methods (glycolaldehyde 1 g, KSCN 3.24 g, water 3 ml, 37% HCl 2.10 ml, RT 2 h then 80 C, 24 h)
steps.notes: pH not reported. From the stated amounts (about 25 mmol HCl in about 5 ml) we calculate pH below 1; recorded as 0 (a bound, our calculation). Product extracted into ethyl acetate and crystallised; the paper notes 2-thiooxazole can also crystallise directly from water and sublime.
assumptions: pH 0 is our calculation from reagent amounts, not a measurement

steps.name: 2-thiooxazole + glyceraldehyde -> pentose oxazolidinone thiones (1a)
steps.yield_text: up to 74% thione 1a in 24 h (70% ribo+arabino 1:1, 30% lyxo/xylo)
steps.where: Results: 'near neutral pH (pH 4-9)... 60 C... up to 74% thione 1a in 24 h'
steps.notes: Works at pH 4-9; sluggish below 6, faster above 7. Recorded at pH 7.

steps.name: thione 1a + cyanoacetylene + ammonia -> arabino- and ribo-aminooxazoline (10a)
steps.yield_text: 15-23% 10a per pass from cyanovinyl thione 1b with NH4Cl 1 M at pH 8.5-10.5; 45% arabino + 33% ribo over two cyanovinylation/ammonolysis cycles at pH 10.5
steps.where: Results 'Aminooxazoline synthesis' (0.24 M 1a, 0.25 M cyanoacetylene, pH 7-10.5; repeated cycles at pH 10.5)
steps.notes: Room temperature (recorded as 25 C). ribo-10a crystallises spontaneously after two cycles. Encoded at pH 9 (inside the 8.5-10.5 range where a yield is reported) to give the route its most favourable reading; output concentrations use the two-cycle pH 10.5 yields, which is generous.
assumptions: pH 9 chosen inside the source's 8.5-10.5 range; the 45/33% yield was at pH 10.5

steps.name: arabino-aminooxazoline + cyanoacetylene -> 2,2'-anhydrocytidine
steps.yield_text: published (Powner 2009) but full text paywalled; not read
steps.where: abstract only; conditions from Stairs 2017's description
steps.notes: Stairs 2017 (10.1038/ncomms15270) states this step needs stoichiometric phosphate to keep pH < 7 and stop hydrolysis of the anhydronucleoside (which hydrolyses readily above pH 6.5). pH recorded as the bound 7.
assumptions: pH 7 is the upper bound '< 7' from Stairs 2017

steps.name: anhydrocytidine + phosphate + urea in formamide -> cytidine-2',3'-cyclic phosphate
steps.yield_text: 44% (co-phosphorylated with 8,2'-anhydro-adenosine, 34%); formamide, 100 C, 72 h
steps.where: Results last paragraph ('44% and 34%'); Methods, phosphorylation Method V
steps.notes: pH not stated. Stairs 2017 also notes significant hydrolysis of 11 under urea-mediated phosphorylation. Powner 2009 phosphorylated by drying an aqueous solution with urea and phosphate (not read).

steps.name: UV: cytidine-2',3'-cyclic phosphate -> uridine-2',3'-cyclic phosphate (partial)
steps.yield_text: published (Powner 2009, Fig. 5) but full text paywalled; not read
steps.where: abstract and figure titles only; Patel 2015 main text says UV 'partially converts'
steps.notes: Patel 2015 (10.1038/nchem.2202) intro: UV partially converts C>p to U>p and destroys stereoisomeric impurities.

steps.name: wet-dry polymerisation of 2',3'-cyclic nucleotides (A, U, G, C) -> RNA oligomers

steps.where: Abstract; Methods (50 mM total, KOH, 23 C, slow evaporation 8-10 h, water only per cycle)
steps.notes: Concentrations are per nucleotide (50 mM equimolar AUGC). RNA_oligomers is in nucleotide equivalents (36% of 50 mM).

routes.label: Alkaline hydrothermal vent
routes.note: Only the first step (CO2 -> formate/acetate) has a published yield.

scenario.name: alkaline_vent
scenario.basis: Altair 2025 (10.1021/jacs.5c01948, Tables 1-2): vent-simulant fluid Na2S 100 mM, K2HPO4 10 mM, Na2Si3O7 10 mM, H2-purged, pH 11, 75 C; ocean simulant Na2Si3O7 10 mM, CO2-purged, pH 5.7, 6 C. Hudson 2020 (10.1073/pnas.2002659117) uses the same vent fluid (pH 12.3) vs ocean pH 3.9. Thermophoresis allowed in vent_chimney/porous_rock (rule), cap 1000x (Matreux 2024, 10.1038/s41586-024-07193-7). The ocean stream's redox class (neutral) is our classification.

steps.name: CO2 + H2 -> formate + acetate across Ni-FeS under pH and thermal gradients
steps.yield_text: formic acid 735.9 uM, acetic acid 11.15 uM after 18 h (ocean 6 C pH 5.7 / vent 75 C pH 11, Ni-FeS)
steps.notes: Engineered set-up: Nafion membrane between compartments, mineral-painted Fe electrodes joined by a wire. At 25 C (Table 1) FeS2 gave 4.2 uM formic + 2.5 uM acetic acid. Hudson 2020 (10.1073/pnas.2002659117) microfluidic, pH 12.3/3.9, room temperature: 1.5 uM formate, none without the pH gradient. Conditions recorded are the ocean side, where product forms.

scenario.name: warm_pond
scenario.basis: Caimi 2025 (10.1021/acscentsci.5c00488): pond with day-night wet-dry cycles, only water added each cycle, room temperature, pH set with KOH. Simonis 2026 (10.1177/15311074261427257, abstract only): Icelandic hot-spring waters (Seltun destructive, Hveradalir benign). Range 0-100 C = liquid water at the surface (our convention). No nucleotide feedstock is supplied by the pond sources.

routes.label: Ice / RNA (QT45, Attwater)
routes.note: Only route with demonstrated template copying; every RNA input is supplied purified.

scenario.name: ice_freeze_thaw
scenario.basis: Gianni 2026 (10.1126/science.adt2760) and Attwater 2025 (10.1038/s41557-025-01830-y): eutectic ice at -7 C, pH 9 (CHES-KOH), 0.4 mM MgCl2; Attwater cycles add HCl (to ~pH 3.6), heat to 80 C for 2 min, add KOH and refreeze. The range -10..80 C is set to the experiments' span; no geological source for this combination was read by us (Attwater cite a geothermal-ice setting; not checked). Mg2+ concentration in a natural setting is not stated (INF).

steps.name: prebiotic synthesis of trinucleotide triphosphates (pppNNN)
steps.yield_text: no published step known to us
steps.notes: Both ice papers use triplets prepared in the laboratory; no prebiotic route was in the sources read.

steps.name: abiotic emergence of a 45-nt polymerase ribozyme (QT45)
steps.yield_text: no published step known to us
steps.notes: QT45 was selected from transcribed random pools; abiotic oligomers reach ~10 nt at 0.1% (Caimi 2025).

steps.name: QT45 copies its complementary strand and itself from triplets in eutectic ice

inputs.note: 50 nM each triplet; 15 defined or all 64
8 nM primer BCy3P10 (template carries a primer-binding site)

steps.yield_text: (-) strand 0.24% and (+) strand 0.17% of template in 72 days; fidelity 94.1%/nt (64-triplet pool); 10.9% perfect full-length (-), 43.4% perfect (+) with defined triplets
steps.where: Abstract; Results 'self-synthesis'; Fig. 4 legend (8 nM primer and template, 80 nM ribozyme, 50 nM each substrate, 0.4 mM MgCl2, 1.2 mM KCl, 1 mM CHES-KOH pH 9, 72 days at -7 C)
steps.notes: (-) and (+) syntheses ran in separate tubes; (+) synthesis needed one pre-formed hexamer and one pH-heat-freeze cycle. Output concentrations = yield x 8 nM template (our arithmetic).

steps.name: pH-freeze-thaw cycling: triplet-based exponential replication of short dsRNA by the TPR ribozyme

inputs.note: 20 nM triplet polymerase ribozyme (5TU + t1 heterodimer); resupplied at each dilution

steps.yield_text: 1.2-1.46-fold per cycle for short (+8 to +14 nt) products; 29-nt ribozyme fragment up to 1.26-fold per cycle; A_D duplex 9x (+) and 31x (-) over 21 cycles
steps.where: Results 'Open-ended RNA amplification', Fig. 3 legend, 'Fragmentary self-replication'; Methods 'Replication cycling'
steps.notes: Each cycle: +0.6 mM HCl, 80 C 2 min, +KOH, flash-freeze in liquid N2, -7 C ~24 h. Freezing concentrates solutes ~440x. A different ribozyme (TPR) from QT45; the whole replicase is not replicated.
